node.title: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes: Principles of biotechnology; Tools of

questions.stem: Restriction enzymes that cut DNA at specific positions within the molecule, away from its ends, are called
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes belong to the class of nucleases, which are of two kinds. Endonucleases cut the DNA at specific positions within the molecule, while exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA. The cutting of DNA at particular recognition sites is therefore done by restriction endonucleases.

optionRationale.2: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA and do not cut at internal sites.
optionRationale.3: Ligases join DNA fragments; they do not cut.
optionRationale.4: Polymerases synthesise new DNA strands; they do not cut at recognition sites.

questions.stem: In the name of the restriction enzyme EcoRI, the letter R stands for
options: the order in which the enzyme was isolated
questions.explanation: The first letter E comes from the genus Escherichia, the next two letters co from the species coli, and R from the strain RY13 of the bacterium. The Roman numeral I shows the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain.

optionRationale.1: The genus is shown by the first letter E.
optionRationale.3: The species is shown by the letters co.
optionRationale.4: The order of isolation is shown by the Roman numeral I.

questions.objective: Decode the nomenclature of restriction enzymes

questions.stem: A plasmid of which bacterium, after modification, is used as a cloning vector to deliver genes into plant cells?
questions.explanation: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of many dicot plants. Its tumour-inducing (Ti) plasmid can deliver a segment called T-DNA into plant cells, so after the tumour-causing genes are removed (disarmed), it serves as a vector for introducing genes into plants.

optionRationale.1: Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of the Bt toxin genes, not the Ti plasmid.
optionRationale.2: Thermus aquaticus is the source of the thermostable Taq polymerase.
optionRationale.4: E. coli is a common host for cloning, but the plant transfer vector comes from Agrobacterium.

questions.objective: Identify the source of the Ti plasmid vector

questions.stem: Which of the following serves as a selectable marker in a cloning vector?
options: A recognition site for a restriction enzyme
A gene for resistance to an antibiotic such as ampicillin
questions.explanation: A selectable marker helps to identify and eliminate non-transformants and to select the transformants. Genes for resistance to antibiotics such as ampicillin, tetracycline or kanamycin act as markers, because only the cells that took up the vector survive when the antibiotic is added to the medium.

optionRationale.1: The origin of replication allows the vector to multiply in the host but does not select transformants.
optionRationale.2: A recognition site is where the foreign DNA is inserted, not a marker.
optionRationale.3: A promoter drives the expression of a gene but does not select transformed cells.

questions.stem: DNA fragments separated on an agarose gel are made visible by staining with
options: ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV light
questions.explanation: After electrophoresis the DNA is stained with ethidium bromide, which binds to the DNA, and the gel is exposed to ultraviolet radiation. The DNA fragments then appear as bright orange coloured bands. Pure DNA fragments can later be cut out from the gel for use in cloning.

optionRationale.1: Acetocarmine is a stain for chromosomes in cytology, not a gel stain for DNA bands.
optionRationale.3: Safranin is a plant histology stain and is not used to visualise DNA bands in a gel.

questions.objective: Recall visualisation of DNA in a gel

questions.stem: The correct order of the three steps repeated in each cycle of PCR is
questions.explanation: In each cycle the double-stranded DNA is first denatured into two single strands by heating. The primers then anneal to the complementary regions of the single strands, and finally Taq polymerase extends the primers using the nucleotides in the reaction. The order is denaturation, annealing, extension.

optionRationale.1: Primers cannot anneal until the strands have been separated by denaturation.
optionRationale.2: Extension needs primers already annealed, so it cannot come first.
optionRationale.3: Extension cannot precede annealing, because the polymerase extends annealed primers.

questions.objective: Sequence the steps of a PCR cycle

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about bioreactors and downstream processing.
A. A bioreactor provides optimal conditions such as temperature, pH, substrate and oxygen for obtaining the desired product.
B. Downstream processing includes the separation and purification of the product.
C. Before marketing, the product is formulated with suitable preservatives and subjected to quality control and clinical trials.
D. Downstream processing is done before the culture is grown in the bioreactor.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: A bioreactor gives optimum conditions of temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins and oxygen for the product, so A is correct. Downstream processing means separation and purification, followed by formulation with preservatives and quality control, so B and C are correct. It follows biosynthesis, so D is false.

optionRationale.1: Statement C is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.2: Statement A is also correct, so this is incomplete.
optionRationale.4: Statement D is false; downstream processing comes after the product is made.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on bioreactors and downstream processing

questions.stem: Match List-I (enzyme used in isolating DNA) with List-II (its action) and choose the correct code.

right: I. Breaks down the fungal cell wall
II. Breaks down the bacterial cell wall
III. Removes RNA from the preparation
IV. Breaks down the plant cell wall

questions.explanation: To release DNA, the cell wall must be broken. Lysozyme digests the bacterial cell wall (A-II), cellulase the plant cell wall (B-IV) and chitinase the fungal cell wall (C-I). Ribonuclease then removes the RNA, so that purer DNA is obtained (D-III).

optionRationale.2: A and B are interchanged; lysozyme acts on bacteria and cellulase on plants.
optionRationale.3: C and D are interchanged; chitinase acts on the fungal wall and ribonuclease on RNA.
optionRationale.4: A and C are interchanged; lysozyme acts on bacteria and chitinase on fungi.

questions.objective: Match enzymes with their action in DNA isolation

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Agarose gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to their size.
Reason (R): DNA is negatively charged because of its phosphate groups.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The negative charge of the phosphate backbone is why all DNA fragments move towards the anode. The separation by size comes from the agarose gel acting as a sieve, since smaller fragments move farther. So both statements are true, but R explains the direction, not the size-based separation.

optionRationale.1: Charge explains why the fragments move towards the anode, not why they are sorted by size; the sieving effect of the gel does that.
optionRationale.3: R is true; the phosphate groups give DNA a net negative charge.
optionRationale.4: A is true; fragments are separated by size in the gel.

questions.objective: Separate the roles of charge and sieving in electrophoresis

questions.stem: A circular plasmid has three recognition sites for a restriction enzyme. The number of fragments produced on complete digestion is
questions.explanation: A circular molecule has no free ends. The first cut only opens the circle into one linear piece, and every further cut adds one more piece. So the number of fragments equals the number of cuts, three here, unlike a linear DNA, where n cuts give n + 1 pieces.

optionRationale.1: Two fragments would result from only two cuts of a circular plasmid.
optionRationale.2: Four fragments are the result of three cuts in a linear DNA, not in a circular one.
optionRationale.4: Six has no basis; the number of fragments equals the number of cuts in a circle.

questions.objective: Count fragments from a circular DNA digest

questions.stem: A linear DNA of 10 kb gives fragments of 2 kb and 8 kb with enzyme X, and 7 kb and 3 kb with enzyme Y. When both enzymes act together the fragments are 2 kb, 5 kb and 3 kb. The distance between the X site and the Y site is
questions.explanation: Enzyme X cuts 2 kb from one end and enzyme Y cuts 3 kb from the other end of the 10 kb molecule. These two sites leave a middle piece of 10 - 2 - 3 = 5 kb, which appears in the double digest as the 5 kb fragment between the two cuts, so the sites lie 5 kb apart.

optionRationale.1: 2 kb is the end fragment cut off by enzyme X, not the distance between the sites.
optionRationale.2: 3 kb is the end fragment cut off by enzyme Y.
optionRationale.3: 7 kb is one of the fragments given by enzyme Y alone, not the gap between the two sites.

questions.objective: Map restriction sites from digest data

questions.stem: Why is the T-DNA of the Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium disarmed before the plasmid is used as a vector?
options: So that it no longer causes tumours but can still transfer DNA to the plant cell
So that the plasmid can replicate in animal cells as well as in plant cells
So that the plasmid can carry many more antibiotic resistance genes
So that the plasmid can be cut by only a single restriction enzyme
questions.explanation: The natural Ti plasmid carries genes that cause tumour formation in the plant. Researchers remove these genes, so that the plasmid is disarmed, but keep the ability of the T-DNA to be transferred into the plant genome. The vector can then deliver a desired gene without causing disease.

optionRationale.2: Disarming does not change the host range of replication; it concerns tumour-causing genes.
optionRationale.3: Disarming does not add antibiotic resistance genes.
optionRationale.4: Disarming has no effect on the number of restriction sites.

questions.objective: Explain the disarming of the Ti plasmid

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about vectors.
A. Plasmids are autonomously replicating, circular, extra-chromosomal DNA of bacteria.
B. Disarmed retroviruses are used to deliver genes into animal cells.
C. The Ti plasmid is used as a vector for delivering genes into plants.
D. A good cloning vector should have many recognition sites for the same restriction enzyme.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Plasmids are circular extra-chromosomal DNA that replicate independently, disarmed retroviruses carry genes into animal cells and the Ti plasmid works in plants, so A, B and C are correct. A vector needs a single recognition site for the enzyme, since many sites would cut it into pieces, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: Statement C is also correct, so this misses it.
optionRationale.3: Statement D is false, and statement A is left out.
optionRationale.4: Statement D is false, and statement B is left out.

questions.stem: DNA fragments of 2 kb, 5 kb and 9 kb are run on an agarose gel. Arranged from the farthest to the nearest to the well, the order of the fragments is
questions.explanation: The gel acts as a sieve and the smaller fragments move more easily through it. The smallest fragment of 2 kb therefore travels the farthest, followed by 5 kb, while the largest fragment of 9 kb stays closest to the well. All the fragments move towards the positive electrode.

optionRationale.1: This reverses the order; the larger fragments move more slowly.
optionRationale.2: The 9 kb fragment is the largest and cannot travel farther than 5 kb or 2 kb.
optionRationale.4: The 5 kb fragment cannot be nearer the well than the 9 kb fragment.

questions.objective: Predict the order of fragments on a gel

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Downstream processing is as important as the production of a biotechnological product in a bioreactor.
Reason (R): The product must be separated, purified and formulated with suitable preservatives, and passed through quality control, before it can be marketed.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The product leaving the bioreactor is mixed with the culture and is not ready for use. Separation, purification, formulation and quality control are required before a protein or other product can be sold, which is why downstream processing is as vital as the biosynthesis itself.

optionRationale.2: R is the very reason downstream processing is important, so it explains A.
optionRationale.3: R is true; formulation and quality control are part of downstream processing.
optionRationale.4: A is true; the product is unusable without downstream processing.

questions.objective: Explain the importance of downstream processing
